title: Ventures Platform Expands with $83M Second Africa Fund to Back Early-Stage Startups
summary: Ventures Platform, a Pan-African venture firm, has raised an $83 million second fund to invest in early-stage startups across Africa, expanding beyond Nigeria to Kenya, South Africa, and Egypt. The firm focuses on sectors like fintech, healthcare, and SaaS, with a strong interest in AI's role in reducing costs and enabling new business models. The fund aims to deploy capital over 3-4 years, with check sizes up to $3 million. The fundraising environment is now more selective, emphasizing capital efficiency, governance, and proven returns. The firm's strategy highlights local market depth and global connectivity as key differentiators.
key_points: Ventures Platform has raised an $83 million second fund, oversubscribed, to invest in early-stage startups across Africa.
The firm is expanding its geographic focus beyond Nigeria to include Kenya, South Africa, and Egypt.
Investment sectors include fintech, healthcare, SaaS, and areas where technology addresses essential needs, with a strong emphasis on AI's transformative potential.
AI is seen as an enabler for new cost structures and business models, not just a feature.
Check sizes will be up to $3 million, with capital deployment planned over 3-4 years.
The fundraising environment is more selective, with LPs demanding evidence of performance, capital efficiency, and governance.
70% of Fund I's LPs returned for Fund II, including institutions like the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development and Norfund.
The firm's edge lies in combining local market depth with global connectivity to support scaling startups.
